summary: A Network Host Status report covering June 19 to June 30, 1972. No testing was done on June 20 because of an attempt to install the new IMP system. It was replaced by RFC 367.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 366 reports ARPANET host status from June 19 through June 30, 1972. It records daily test results and explains that testing was skipped on June 20 during an attempt to install a new IMP system.

subtitle: A report of ARPANET host status from June 19 to June 30, 1972.

tldr.problem: ARPANET users needed recent information about host availability and the roles of networked systems.
tldr.mechanism: The report lists host roles and daily test results for June 19 through June 30, with no test on June 20 during an IMP system installation attempt.
tldr.outcome: RFC 366 updates RFC 362 and was later obsoleted by RFC 367.

today: RFC 366 updates RFC 362 and was later obsoleted by RFC 367.

sections.title: Report Scope and Host Roles
sections.content:
The RFC reports on most Network Hosts from June 19 to June 30. It says no testing was done on June 20 because of an attempt to install the new IMP system.

The report excludes Terminal IMPs intended as users only and the Network Control Center computer, which was used solely to gather network statistics. It also lists other hosts that were intended to be users only.
sections.plainLanguage: This report covers most network hosts for the second half of June. It leaves out user-only systems and has no tests for June 20 because of an IMP installation attempt.

sections.title: Daily Test Results
sections.content:
The daily table records results for each tested host on listed dates. It uses O for Open, D for Dead, H for Half Open, R for Refused, T for Timed out, and F for Full. Full means that the host opened a connection, told the user all Network ports were in use, and immediately closed the connection.

Timed out means the host did not complete the ICP and open a connection within 60 seconds. A marker identifies sites that had announced they might be unavailable at those times.
sections.plainLanguage: The test codes describe how each host responded, including whether it opened, refused, or timed out. A timeout means the connection did not open within 60 seconds.

sections.title: Status and Prediction Table
sections.content:
A separate table lists host status or predictions and the person providing each report. It includes labels such as Server, User Only, and Soon. The report identifies a Terminal IMP at Lincoln as a user-only system not included in daily testing.

These reported roles and predictions are distinct from the daily connection test results shown in the other table.
sections.plainLanguage: One table shows test results; another gives reported roles and predictions. The report keeps those two kinds of information separate.
